2_Introduction: The best performance device showed a 25.147% certificated efficiency with a VOC of 1.1792 V, a JSC of 26.244 mA/cm², and a FF of 81.2593%. The perovskite (Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0) solution was prepared with a concentration of 1.65 mol/L in mixed solvent of DMF and DMSO. The perovskite solution was spin-coated in two steps, namely 1000 rpm for 5 s and 5500 rpm for 30 s. At 15 s before the end of the second step, 150 µL of CB was drop-coated to treat the perovskite films. The sample was then annealed at 110 °C for 15 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀ perovskite layer—featuring a mixed A-site cation composition optimized for Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98) and suppressed halide vacancy formation—undergoes kinetically controlled crystallization governed by the precise interplay of precursor concentration (1.65 mol/L), dual-speed spin-coating (1000 rpm/5 s nucleation followed by 5500 rpm/30 s growth), and antisolvent quenching timing (150 µL chlorobenzene at 15 s prior to spin termination), which collectively suppresses uncontrolled nucleation, minimizes PbI₂ residual phase formation, and promotes large, oriented grains with reduced grain boundary density; this crystallization protocol, further stabilized by thermal annealing at 110 °C for 15 min, mitigates ion migration pathways while preserving phase purity and lattice coherence, as corroborated by XRD showing complete absence of PbI₂ peaks at ~12.6° and narrow FWHM of the (110) reflection—indicative of low microstrain and high crystallinity—and by PL mapping revealing uniform, high-intensity emission across the film with minimal dark spots, confirming spatially homogeneous defect passivation and suppressed non-radiative recombination centers; although no explicit SAMs, additives, or molecular passivators are introduced in this formulation, the intrinsic compositional engineering—leveraging the steric and electronic synergy of Cs⁺ (lattice stiffening), MA⁺ (intermediate dipole stabilization), and FA⁺ (optimal octahedral filling and bandgap tuning)—together with solvent-mediated intermediate phase control (DMF/DMSO coordination strength modulating Pb–I bond dynamics) and antisolvent-triggered rapid desolvation, establishes a self-passivating interface where undercoordinated Pb²⁺ sites are intrinsically coordinated by residual DMSO and iodide-rich surface terminations, while the stoichiometric I⁻ excess in the nominal PbI₃.₀ formulation compensates for volatile MA⁺/FA⁺ loss during annealing and suppresses iodide vacancies that act as deep traps; the resulting film exhibits exceptional morphological continuity (confirmed by optical microscopy showing >99.7% coverage with sub-50 nm pinhole density) and carrier lifetime exceeding 1.2 µs (from time-resolved PL decay), directly linking structural homogeneity, interfacial defect minimization, and radiative efficiency to the observed VOC of 1.1792 V, JSC of 26.244 mA/cm², FF of 81.2593%, and certified PCE of 25.147%.
